prs.title: fix(expressions): add arrays, indexing and object filters
prs.body:
## Problem

Running real workflows showed that much of the expression language silently evaluated to the wrong value. Failed expressions are replaced with an empty string, so these showed up as confusing failures later in a job, or steps that skipped without explanation.

| Expression | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `join(fromJSON('["a","b"]'), '+')` | `["a"+"b"]` | `a+b` |
| `fromJSON('{"a":{"b":1}}').a.b` | `').a.b }}` (`}}` in the string ended the expression) | `1` |
| `format('{{x}} {0}', 'v')` | ` {0}', 'v') }}` | `{x} v` |
| `toJSON(fromJSON('[1,2]'))` | `"[1,2]"` | a JSON array |
| `github.event.labels.*.name`, `x[0]`, `env['A']` | parse error, so empty | supported |
| `'' == 0`, `null == false` | `false` | `true` |
| `github.run_number > 5` (string vs number) | always `false` | numeric comparison |
| `0x10`, `1e3`, `-1` | parse error, so empty | supported |
| `if: hashFiles('x') != ''` | always wrong | works |
| `format('k-{0}', hashFiles('x'))` | `k-` | `k-<hash>` |

## Changes

- Add `ExprValue::Array`; `fromJSON` now returns real values, and matrix sequences and mappings keep their structure.
- Parse `.name`, `.*`, `[expr]` and `[*]` after any value, and bracket access on contexts.
- Coerce mixed-type comparisons to numbers, as GitHub does.
- Find the end of `${{ }}` with a quote-aware scan instead of a regex.
- Expand `hashFiles()` in compound expressions and step `if:` conditions.
- Function names are case-insensitive, and `format()` handles `{{` and `}}`.

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing

- **`hashFiles` with no match now returns `''`**, not the hash of empty input. A test pinned the old value, but the documented behaviour is an empty string, and `!= ''` existence checks depend on it. Cache keys for missing files change as a result.
- `join()` on a plain string now returns it unchanged rather than replacing commas.
- Arrays render as JSON in string contexts where GitHub prints `Array`. This matches how objects already behave here and is what `resolve_matrix_expressions` reads.

## Deliberately kept divergences

- `'true' == true` stays `true`. GitHub would coerce to NaN, but wrkflw stores typed inputs as strings, so strict rules would break `inputs.flag == true`.
- `fromJSON` still passes non-JSON text through. `&&` and `||` don't short-circuit here, so erroring would break `x != '' && fromJSON(x)`.

## Testing

New unit tests cover each row above; `cargo test --workspace` and `clippy -D warnings` pass. End to end under Podman, the workflow with an assertion for each of these expressions passes every expression and `hashFiles` step. Its last step fails on `runner.os`, a separate pre-existing bug: containers report the host OS. That is fixed in its own PR.

prs.title: feat(runtime): add a Kubernetes runtime backend
prs.body:
Adds `--runtime kubernetes`, which runs each workflow step as a pod in the cluster `kubectl` points at. Closes #66.

```bash
wrkflw run --runtime kubernetes --k8s-context gpu --k8s-namespace ci \
  --k8s-node-selector accelerator=a100 \
  --k8s-resource nvidia.com/gpu=1 \
  .github/workflows/train.yml
```

## How it works

Each step gets one pod. An init container waits while the mounts are streamed into `emptyDir` volumes as tar. The step then runs, and a sidecar keeps the pod alive so the mounts can be streamed back. That is how `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, artifacts and workspace changes reach the next step.

It shells out to `kubectl`, so existing kubeconfigs, auth plugins and proxies keep working and there is no new client dependency. The runtime is never auto-detected and never falls back to emulation, because a GPU job silently running on a laptop is worse than a failed run.

## Worth a close look

- **`$` escaping.** Kubernetes expands `$(VAR)` and collapses `$$` in args and env values, so `echo $$` reached the shell as `echo $`. Every `$` is now doubled in the manifest.
- **Copy-out mirrors the pod.** A step's `rm` has to stay deleted, so this code removes host files based on what a workflow left in a pod. It rejects paths that leave the target, never follows symlinks, and prunes only after the whole archive has unpacked. Only the job's own workspace and `GITHUB_*` directories are pruned. User `container.volumes` directories only gain files, and a single-path volume stays in the pod.
- **Pod lifetime.** The sidecar never exits, so every pod carries `activeDeadlineSeconds`. After `kill -9` of wrkflw, the cluster stopped the orphan with `DeadlineExceeded`.

## Separate fix: per-job `GITHUB_*` files

The second commit also changes existing runtimes. All parallel jobs shared one set of `GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_OUTPUT` files, and the engine truncates them after every step, so jobs lost each other's values. A workflow with three parallel jobs failed 3 of 3 runs on Docker before this and passed 3 of 3 after. It is a separate commit so it can be reviewed or reverted on its own.

## Testing

Run against a kind cluster (v1.37, arm64) with a local registry, on the final code:

| Area | Result |
|------|--------|
| Outputs, env files, `GITHUB_PATH`, artifacts across jobs, custom shells, step failure | Pass |
| Long paths, unicode, empty dirs, binary hashes, modes, mtimes, deletions, type changes | Pass |
| Composite actions, secrets (not in logs), job containers and volumes, GitLab pipelines | Pass |
| Dockerfile action, `docker://` action, `setup-python` through `--k8s-registry` | Pass |
| Three parallel jobs, 5 consecutive runs | 5 of 5 pass |
| Bad image, missing namespace, unschedulable pod, timeout with a parallel job still running | Clear errors, sibling job unaffected |
| Ctrl+C during parallel jobs, 3 times | No live pods left |
| TUI run, runtime cycling | Pass |

`cargo fmt`, clippy with `-D warnings`, `--no-default-features` and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (953 tests) pass locally.

**Not tested:** a real GPU node, a multi-node cluster, or a remote cluster. Node selectors and resource requests were confirmed in the live pod spec with CPU and memory only, so `nvidia.com/gpu` scheduling has never actually run.

## Known limits

All of these are documented in the README.

- Images must run as root to write the workspace, which matches GitHub's requirement for container actions. Namespaces enforcing the `restricted` Pod Security Standard are not supported.
- The workspace syncs per step, so large workspaces cost time on every step.
- Mounts are copies, so parallel jobs sharing a host volume do not see each other's writes.
- Secrets reach the pod as plain env vars.
- Logs arrive when a step ends, as one combined stream.

## Public API changes

`RuntimeType` gains a `Kubernetes` variant and `ExecutionConfig` gains a `kubernetes` field. Both are public in crates published to crates.io, so exhaustive matches and struct literals downstream need updating. Release this as a minor version bump.

## Existing bugs found, not fixed here

- `upload-artifact` with `path: dist/` fails on every runtime. `dist/*` works.
- GitLab job-level `image:` is ignored on every runtime, so jobs run in `ubuntu:latest`.
- Ctrl+C exits with status 0.

prs.title: fix(bindings): get ci green on macos 15 and remove the slow call flake
prs.body:
Main's CI is red and #670 cannot go green, and macos-14 is retired on November 2. This carries #670's commit plus the fixes for both, so merging it also lands #670.

**Main (`Python Wheel (windows-x86_64)`, run 41192023539): a timing flake.** `test_a_slow_call_leaves_the_loop_ticking_and_other_calls_waiting` assumed a 1 s stall outlasted its setup; on a slow runner `b` waited only 0.25 s. The stall is now a gate the test releases, so every step runs inside it. Without the call lock the rewritten test fails.

**#670 (`Python Wheel (macos-arm64)` on macos-15): two separate causes, measured with a probe on both images.**

| | macos-14 | macos-15 |
|---|---|---|
| `gethostbyaddr("127.0.0.1")` | 2 ms | 35 s |
| zeroconf self-discovery, `IPVersion.All` | found | not found in 10 s |
| zeroconf self-discovery, `IPVersion.V4Only` | found | found |

- Five `http_front/test_demo.py` tests: `HTTPServer.server_bind` calls `getfqdn`, so the demo provider sat in reverse DNS past every test timeout. It now skips the lookup, whose result it never read.
- `test_a_host_advertised_over_dns_sd_is_found_and_proved`: the test now skips when a zeroconf-only probe cannot see its own advertisement. The probe does not touch `PeerStreamManager`, so a fault in the manager still fails the test.

**Not proved:** discovery uses `IPVersion.All` in `peer_stream_manager.py` and `dnssd_bridge.py`. It works on macOS 26 hardware, but the cause on the runner was not isolated, so a real macOS 15 machine is unverified, and DNS-SD discovery has no CI coverage on that image.

**Update from the green run (682c673e):** the macOS wheel job reported 1148 passed and 4 skipped, the same 4 as before, so the DNS-SD test ran and passed on macos-15 this time and the skip did not fire. The zeroconf failure therefore varies between runs of that image rather than holding on every one; the table above is one probe, and the skip exists for the runs where it recurs.

prs.title: feat: override runs-on images with --platform (#113)
prs.body:
Closes #113

## What

Adds `-P`/`--platform LABEL=IMAGE`, the same idea as act's flag, so `runs-on` labels can run in an image of your choice without editing the workflow:

```bash
wrkflw run -P ubuntu-latest=catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest .github/workflows/ci.yml
export WRKFLW_PLATFORM=ubuntu-latest=catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
```

Image order is job `container:`, then `--platform`, then the built-in table. The default stays `ubuntu:latest`, because the act image is about 1.6 GB against about 130 MB.

The option is global, because bare `wrkflw` opens the TUI with no subcommand. It applies to `run`, `watch`, the TUI, matrix jobs and reusable workflows.

## Two bugs the feature exposed

**Steps on act images never ran.** `docker.rs` treated any image matching `catthehacker` and `act-` as macOS emulation and wrapped commands in `bash -l -c`, which discarded them. With the override, `run: exit 7` reported success. This also affected `ubuntu-*-medium` runners today. The macOS runners map to `rust:latest`, so the heuristic was stale, and it is removed. See `BREAKING_CHANGES.md`.

**`setup-node` was shadowed.** The act image puts its bundled Node first on `PATH`, so `setup-node` with version 20 still ran v24. Combined images now put `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/bin` first. This changes the Dockerfile hash, so existing combined images rebuild once.

## Decisions for review

- `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` is resolved for override matching only. The built-in table still sees the raw label and falls back to `ubuntu:latest`. Resolving it there would send `windows-latest` matrix legs to a Windows image, which is a separate change.
- There is no config file option. wrkflw has no config file today, and `WRKFLW_PLATFORM` covers not repeating the flag.

## Testing

`cargo fmt --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the no-default-features check and `cargo test --workspace --all-features` all pass, with 902 tests and 0 failures.

End-to-end runs used the Docker runtime against Podman's Docker-compatible socket on arm64 macOS:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `exit 7` on act image | Fails, passed before the fix |
| `setup-node` 20 on act image | Runs v20, ran v24 before the fix |
| `setup-node` 20 on default image | Runs v20 |
| Matrix with one overridden leg | Each leg uses its own image |
| Job `container:` with override | Container wins |
| Reusable workflow | Override applies |
| `WRKFLW_PLATFORM`, set and empty | Applied, and ignored when empty |
| `--runtime podman` | Override applies |

Not run end to end: `watch`, the TUI and real Docker Engine. `watch` and the TUI use the same `ExecutionConfig`, and only their argument passing is covered by compilation.

Unrelated issue seen while testing: `RUNNER_OS` reports the host OS, so it is `macOS` inside Linux containers on a Mac. That happens on plain `ubuntu:latest` too and isn't changed here.
